title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

plan.title: Too much of one thing, none of another
Why you hold on the way you do
How you fight, and how you say sorry (or don't)
How you show love vs how you need it
Yeon's red flag report on you
What you need (not what you chase)

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. When you fall, you don't wait for permission. You decide, then inform them.

Bom: It's so flattering to be chosen like that.

Yeon: It's flattering in week one. By week six they'd like a vote.

Let the next one catch up. Ask one question a date that you don't already know the answer to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fall in love. You announce it.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You fall by melting. Their laugh, their texts, the way they said your name once.

Yeon: And then you shape yourself around them before they've even asked for anything.

Bom: Falling soft is lovely. Losing yourself isn't part of the deal.

Keep one thing that's only yours while you fall. A class, a friend night, a Sunday ritual. Protect it like it's a date.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fall softly. Just keep your own floor under you.

strong.text:
Built strong, so you flirt like someone who expects it to work. Annoyingly, it usually does.

Yeon: The risk: you read a polite laugh as a yes, and keep going past the point where they were still deciding.

Bom: You're not pushy. You're confident.

Yeon: Confident people can still leave a gap. Say the charming thing, then stop. Let them walk toward you.

A pause is wildly underrated. Ask a question and wait through the whole answer. Being a little less available for one beat makes everything you do say land harder.

Bom: And notice when you're flirting to win. To be the most interesting person in the room, to prove you've still got it.

Yeon: Performing for an audience of twelve is not the same as connecting with one. Turn the volume down. Ask them something real.

Bom: Speaking of volume, next chapter is what your chart has too much of. It shows up on dates more than you'd think.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One charming line. Then shut up and let them close the gap.

weak.text:
Built soft, so your flirting is quiet. So quiet that half the time they don't know it's happening.

Bom: You hint. A longer look. Remembering what they said last week. Laughing a bit more than the joke deserved.

Yeon: And then you wait for them to decode it. Babe, they don't have the key.

Bom: Soft flirting is lovely. It just needs one clear signal attached.

One sentence that can't be misread. "I'd like to see you again." "I was hoping you'd be here." Plain, warm, done.

Yeon: The scary part lasts four seconds. The not-knowing you're doing now lasts months.

Bom: And if they don't respond the way you hoped? That's an answer too. Answers are kinder than months of maybe. People who'd be good for you love being chosen out loud.

Yeon: Next chapter, what your chart overdoes and what it skips. Both explain why you hint instead of saying.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keep the soft flirting. Add one sentence they can't misread.

strong.text:
Built strong, so when you hold on, you hold on with a plan.

Yeon: They go quiet for a day and you don't panic. You manage. Suggestions, check-ins, a helpful little restructure of their week.

Bom: It comes from caring. You want it to work.

Yeon: It lands as "I am now project-managing your feelings."

Strong charts trust themselves more than they trust the space between two people. So you fill the space. With logistics, with reassurance nobody asked for, with fixing.

Bom: Try letting a quiet day just be a quiet day.

Yeon: No investigation. No pep talk. No "so, are we good?" at 11pm.

Bom: People who feel trusted move closer on their own. Give them the chance to prove it.

Yeon: And ask yourself who manages you when you wobble. If the answer is nobody, that's the real work.

Bom: Let someone in on the planning. Let them hold you up for once.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A quiet day is not a crisis to manage. Leave it alone.

weak.text:
Built soft, so you hold on by holding still. Being easy, being available, being no trouble at all.

Bom: You worry that needing things will make them leave.

Yeon: So you need nothing, visibly, and then cry in the shower about it. Very efficient.

Soft charts often confuse relief with love. Someone texts back and the relief is so strong it feels like chemistry.

Bom: Relief isn't the same as being happy with someone. Notice the difference.

Yeon: Ask for one small thing this week. A call instead of a text. A plan that's yours.

Bom: The right person says yes and feels closer for it. That's the test, and you're allowed to run it.

Yeon: If the answer is a sulk or a sigh, you've learned something important early. Cheap lesson.

Bom: Better a small no in month two than a big silence in year two.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Relief when they text back isn't the same as love. Notice which one it is.

strong.text:
Built strong, so your jealousy comes out as control and calls itself standards.

Yeon: "I just think it's weird that they text you that much." Said casually. Rehearsed four times.

Bom: You feel things strongly, and you protect what's yours.

Yeon: People aren't yours, babe. They're with you. Different preposition, different relationship.

When it hits, name the feeling, not their behaviour. "I felt left out tonight" lands. "Why do you always" starts a war.

Bom: And ask what you actually need. Usually it's reassurance, not a new rule. You're allowed to want to feel special. Everyone does.

Yeon: Wanting it is fine. Policing it isn't. Rules make people sneaky. Reassurance makes them stay.

Bom: Next chapter: what happens when the jealousy turns into a fight, and how you say sorry. Or don't.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Name the feeling, not the crime. "I felt left out" beats "why do you always."

weak.text:
Built soft, so your jealousy goes inward and turns into a quiet audit of yourself.

Bom: They mention a coworker and you spend the evening comparing. Their hair, their job, their laugh.

Yeon: Then you say "no, I'm fine" and go to bed doing maths about your own worth.

Bom: It's not that you're insecure. You just don't feel chosen often enough.

Tell them, early and small. "Can you remind me I'm your favourite? I'm having a wobble." Most partners are relieved to be asked.

Yeon: It's a lot less dramatic than three days of silence followed by tears over a pasta sauce.

Bom: Ask for the reminder. Then believe it when it comes.

Yeon: And stop comparing yourself to people they've barely mentioned. You're competing with a ghost you invented. Next chapter, how that wobble turns into an actual fight. You'll recognise it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "Remind me I'm your favourite?" Say it. Most partners love being asked.

strong.text:
Built strong, so your red flag comes with a strong defence.

Yeon: Someone points it out and you've got context, history and a counter-example ready. Usually about them.

Bom: You don't like feeling cornered.

Yeon: Nobody does. But a partner who brings it up is trying to stay, not leave.

Next time, say "you might be right, let me think about it." Then actually think about it. Out of their sight, if you must.

Bom: Strong charts improve fast once they stop arguing with the feedback. "I'm working on it" is one of the most attractive sentences there is.

Yeon: Followed by actually working on it. Otherwise it's just a nice sentence. Next chapter is what you really need, which, spoiler, isn't what you keep chasing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Swap the counter-example for "let me sit with that." Then sit with it.

weak.text:
Built soft, so your red flag is that you stay too long.

Yeon: Something stopped working in March. It's October. You're still explaining it to your friends as "a phase."

Bom: You're loyal. You see potential.

Yeon: You see potential like it's a lease you can't break.

Soft charts tend to measure love by how much they can tolerate. That's endurance, and it gets mistaken for devotion.

Bom: Love shouldn't feel like a test of how much you can take. If a friend described this relationship to you, what would you tell them?

Yeon: Now tell yourself that. Same tone. Same love. And read the next chapter twice: it's what you need instead.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Potential isn't a lease. You're allowed to leave a phase that's lasted a year.

strong.text:
Bom's addition for strong charts: you need someone who isn't scared of you.

Yeon: Not scared of your opinions, your plans, or your face when you disagree.

Bom: You do best with someone who says "no, I don't think so" calmly, and then still hugs you.

Yeon: Harder to find than you'd think. Most people just agree with you to save time.

So when someone pushes back kindly, notice it. Don't flinch, don't win. That's the person to keep talking to.

Bom: You're worth arguing with. And worth staying for after.

Yeon: And someone with a life big enough that you're not their only project. Or they yours.

Bom: Two full lives that choose to overlap. That's the dream for you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Find someone who says "no" calmly and still hugs you after. Keep them.

weak.text:
Bom's addition for soft charts: you need someone who notices before you have to ask.

Yeon: You'll never ask. So yes, you need a noticer.

Bom: The person who sees you're tired and puts the kettle on. Who remembers the thing you mentioned once.

Yeon: And until you find them, you practise asking anyway. "I'd love a hug." "Can we stay in tonight?"

Being noticed is wonderful. Being able to ask is what keeps you safe while you wait for it.

Bom: Care isn't a prize for being low-maintenance. You can simply receive it.

Yeon: Meanwhile, notice who already does this. A friend, a sibling, the coworker who brings you coffee. That's what good care feels like. Calibrate to it.

Bom: Then don't settle for less in love.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You need a noticer. Until then, practise asking. Out loud.

peer_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {dm_el}, your own element. In saju that's the peer family: equals, friends, rivals.

Yeon: In love it means you want a partner, not a parent and definitely not a project. And you can turn competitive when you feel outranked.

Bom: Over tiny things. Who's busier. Who gave up more. Who's more tired.

Yeon: Nobody else knew there was a scoreboard.

The gift: you never disappear into a relationship. You keep your own life, your own friends, your own opinions.

Bom: The work: letting closeness feel like teamwork instead of a match you're trying to win.

Yeon: Good test for anyone new. Do they have plans that don't include you, and are you glad about it? If yes, you've found an equal, not a rival.

Bom: And when they win something, a promotion, a race, an argument with their mum, celebrate like it's yours.

Yeon: Because in a good relationship, it sort of is.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. You want an equal. Stop racing them to the car.

output_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} pours out. In saju that's output: charm, play, saying it out loud.

Bom: In love you're expressive, funny, the one who sends the voice note and plans the surprise.

Yeon: And the one who gets bored the second the dating becomes a relationship.

Bom: You love the sparkle.

Yeon: You love the sparkle and leave before the dishes. Output-heavy charts often confuse novelty with chemistry.

When it starts to feel routine, don't reach for someone new. Reach for something new with them. A trip, a class, a ridiculous project.

Bom: Same person, fresh chapter. It's surprisingly romantic.

Yeon: Also, the funny one doesn't get a pass on the serious talks. Do the jokes after.

Bom: Your playfulness is a gift. Let it carry the relationship through the boring bits, not out of them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: bored by month four? Try something new with them, not someone new.

wealth_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} pursues and manages. Saju calls it the wealth family. In love it means the chase.

Yeon: You like a challenge. Someone hard to get. Slightly out of reach.

Bom: You go after what you want. That's attractive.

Yeon: Until you get it. Then you start managing it. Their schedule, their style, their five-year plan.

Bom: The chase and the management feel like love to you.

Yeon: They're the before and after of love. The middle is just being with someone without improving them.

Practise the middle. A whole evening where you don't fix, plan or chase anything.

Bom: Some of the managing is worry. If they're fine without your help, you're scared you'll stop mattering.

Yeon: You won't. You'll just get to be their partner instead of their consultant.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The chase is fun. Managing them after isn't love. Try the middle.

power_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that disciplines your {dm_el}. Saju's power family: rules, duty, standards.

Bom: In love you're committed, serious and deeply reliable. If you say you'll call, you call.

Yeon: And you expect the same. To the minute. With a mental note when they don't.

Bom: You just take love seriously.

Yeon: Seriously enough that partners can feel like they're on probation.

Strong charts with heavy power often love through standards. That's safe for you and tiring for them.

Bom: Try praising before correcting. Every time.

Yeon: And let them be late once without a lecture. Love survives lateness. It doesn't survive feeling graded.

Bom: And notice how hard you are on yourself when you slip.

Yeon: Your partner sees it. It's not motivating. It's sad. Be kinder to you, and everyone around you relaxes.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Love through standards is lovely. Love on probation isn't. Praise first.

resource_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. Saju's resource family: comfort, learning, being cared for.

Yeon: In love you research. You read about attachment styles. You know your love language. You have a theory about your ex.

Bom: You're so self-aware.

Yeon: Self-aware, and still on the sofa. Knowing everything about love is not the same as risking any of it.

Bom: You also like being looked after, and you pick partners who do that.

Yeon: Then you get comfortable and stop showing up. Comfort turns into autopilot fast.

Do one brave romantic thing this month. Say the thing. Plan the date. Make the first move.

Bom: Insight is lovely. Action is romantic.

Yeon: Nobody ever swooned because their partner had a really thorough understanding of attachment theory.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've read every book on love. Try one brave move off the page.

output_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} gives out. On a soft chart, output drains you.

Bom: In love you give and give. Attention, effort, humour, the perfect gift.

Yeon: And then you're empty, and you can't work out why you feel lonely in a relationship you're carrying alone.

Bom: You love by pouring out. It's lovely.

Yeon: It's lovely until the jug's dry.

Notice whether anything comes back. A text you didn't start. A plan you didn't make. Effort you didn't have to ask for.

Bom: If nothing comes back, that's information.

Yeon: Not a cue to try harder.

Bom: Give a little less this week and watch who steps up.

Yeon: The ones who step up are keepers. The ones who don't notice were never really looking.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You pour and pour. Check if anything pours back.

wealth_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} tries to hold. On a soft chart, that means taking on more than you can carry.

Yeon: In love you take on their stress, their family drama, their unpaid emotional bills.

Bom: You want them to be okay.

Yeon: You want them okay so badly you've stopped checking if you are.

Soft charts with heavy wealth often pick people who need a lot. It feels like purpose. It ends up feeling like a second job.

Bom: You're allowed to want someone who's already okay.

Yeon: Someone who can hold their own bags. And occasionally yours.

Bom: Notice how it feels to be with someone who asks how you are and actually waits.

Yeon: If that feels strange, that's not a sign it's wrong. It's a sign it's new.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: carrying their stuff and yours. Put some down. Find someone who carries too.

power_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that pressures your {dm_el}. On a soft chart it feels like being judged all the time.

Bom: In love you worry you're not enough. Not pretty enough, smart enough, interesting enough.

Yeon: So you try to be perfect, and perfect people are exhausting to date. Including for themselves.

Bom: All you want is to be chosen.

Yeon: You are chosen. You keep reapplying for the position.

Notice when you're performing instead of being. Then stop performing for one evening and see what happens.

Bom: The right person likes you best with your shoes off.

Yeon: Perfect is boring anyway. Nobody falls for the laminated version.

Bom: They fall for the laugh you make when you trip on the stairs.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You keep reapplying for a job you already have. Sit down.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Bom: In love this shows up as looking more sure than you feel.

Yeon: You seem confident on dates. Then you lie awake rerunning everything you said, forty times.

Bom: People think you don't need much reassurance. You need quite a lot. You just hide it well.

Tell the person you're seeing. "I look calm, but I like hearing that you're into me." Simple. Rarely said. Hugely effective.

Yeon: Nobody falls out of love because you asked for a compliment.

Bom: The right person likes being asked. It tells them they matter to you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look sure. You feel wobbly. Ask for the reassurance. It's allowed.

output_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's expression: how love gets said out loud.

Yeon: So you love in actions and silence. You'd fight anyone for them. You won't say you missed them.

Bom: They feel your love, though.

Yeon: They'd like to hear it. They shouldn't have to infer it from a fixed bike.

Start small. One sentence before bed. A note in their bag. A voice message on the way home.

Bom: Expression gets easier with reps. Like everything you've ever trained.

Writing counts. A card. A text that says more than "ok." A voice note that's not about logistics.

Yeon: And next chapter, why you hold on the way you do. The silence is part of it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fixed their bike. Lovely. Now the words.

wealth_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's pursuit: going after what you want.

Bom: So you're powerful but passive in love. You wait to be chosen.

Yeon: You stand in the corner of the party looking magnificent and hoping someone notices.

Bom: People do notice. They think you're out of reach.

Yeon: Make the first move once. Ask for the number. Suggest the drink.

Strong charts without wealth have all the confidence and none of the initiative.

Yeon: Being admired from across the room is lovely. Being asked out is better. Do the asking.

Bom: Borrow some. Then turn the page. Why you hold on, and why you wait, are related.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: magnificent in the corner. Walk over. Say hi.

power_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's limits and outside structure.

Yeon: In love, that means you make your own rules. You text when you feel like it. You show up when it suits.

Bom: You're free. It's part of your charm.

Yeon: It's charming until they're waiting for a reply you forgot to send. For two days.

Partners need some predictability to feel safe. Pick one thing you'll always do. A goodnight text. A Sunday call.

Bom: Small reliability is a huge love language.

Yeon: Freedom with a goodnight text is still freedom. Promise. Next chapter is how you attach. Spoiler: loosely, until you suddenly don't.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: love on your own schedule. Pick one thing you always do.

resource_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's being looked after.

Bom: You're the strong one. You look after partners. You don't let them look after you.

Yeon: They try. You say "I'm fine." They stop trying. You feel unsupported. Lovely loop.

Bom: You just don't know how to receive.

Yeon: Then practise. Let them pay. Let them cook. Let them hold you when you're sad, without apologising.

Receiving is a skill, not a weakness.

Yeon: Watch the urge to say "I've got it." You don't always have to have it.

Bom: And it's at the heart of the next chapter: how you hold on, and why.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you never let them care for you. Let them cook. Say thank you.

output_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's expression. On a soft chart it keeps your feelings very, very private.

Bom: You feel enormous things. You show tiny ones.

Yeon: A whole love story in your head. A thumbs-up emoji in real life.

Bom: It's safer that way.

Yeon: Safer, and lonelier. They can't love the you they've never met.

Say one true feeling a week. Even small. "I loved tonight."

Yeon: Tiny counts. "I missed you today." Four words. Revolutionary for you.

Bom: Next chapter, why you hold on so tight to things you never said.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Feelings: enormous. Messages: one emoji. Send one real sentence.

wealth_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's pursuit. On a soft chart, you wait to be found.

Yeon: You wait for them to text first. To ask you out. To define the relationship.

Bom: Too keen feels risky, you think.

Yeon: Meanwhile someone keener gets the date.

Make the first move once this month. Small. A message. An invitation.

Bom: Being keen isn't embarrassing. It's honest.

Yeon: The worst outcome is a polite no. You've survived worse. You've survived group projects. Now, next chapter: why you hold on once you've finally got someone.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you wait to be chosen. Choose first, just once.

power_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's outside pressure. On a soft chart, it means fewer rules to lean on.

Bom: In love you go with the flow. Whatever they want, whenever.

Yeon: Which means you never quite say what you want. Exclusivity? Moving in? "Whatever feels right."

Bom: You don't want to pressure anyone.

Yeon: Saying what you want isn't pressure. It's information.

Set one gentle boundary this month. "I'd like us to be exclusive." "I need a reply within a day."

Yeon: A clear want gives the right person something to say yes to.

Bom: And next, how you attach when there's nothing to hold on to.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: "whatever feels right" isn't a want. Say the real one.

resource_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's nourishment. On a soft chart it can leave you hungry for care.

Bom: That's why a little attention feels like so much. One kind text and you're halfway in love.

Yeon: And why you stay in things that feed you crumbs. Crumbs feel like a meal when you're starving.

Bom: Feed yourself first. Friends, rest, things that make you feel good.

Yeon: Then crumbs look like crumbs.

Love from a fuller place picks better.

Yeon: A good partner should add to a full life, not be the only meal in it.

Bom: Next chapter: how that hunger shapes the way you hold on.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Crumbs feel like a feast when you're hungry. Eat elsewhere first.

none_strong.text:
All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars.

Yeon: In love, that means you can be anything. Passionate, patient, playful, steady.

Bom: You have so much range.

Yeon: And you keep picking one setting. The one that worked last time, even if this person needs another.

Notice what the person in front of you responds to. Then try the setting you rarely use.

Yeon: The setting you rarely use might be exactly the one they've been waiting for.

Bom: You have the whole palette. Paint with more than one colour, and turn the page: next chapter is why you hold on the way you do.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: All five elements. One setting on repeat. Try another.

none_weak.text:
All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars.

Bom: You have everything you need to love well. Warmth, steadiness, playfulness, clarity.

Yeon: You just hide most of it, in case it's too much.

Bom: It won't be too much.

Yeon: Show one more colour this month. Say the thing. Plan the date. Be silly first.

You're more than the careful version you lead with.

Yeon: Too much is a fear, not a fact. The right person wants all of it.

Bom: Next chapter is how you hold on. You'll see the careful version there too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: All five elements, and you show one. Show another.

resource.title: What keeps you steady in love: {helper_el}
resource.text:
Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. For a soft {dm_el} chart, it's {helper_el}, the one that feeds you.

Bom: In love, it's the difference between loving from a full cup and loving from an empty one.

Yeon: Empty-cup love picks badly. It mistakes relief for chemistry and crumbs for commitment.

Bom: With enough {helper_el} in your life, you choose more freely and ask with less fear.

Yeon: Quick check before any big relationship decision. Have I slept, eaten, and talked to someone who loves me this week? If not, refuel first. Decide after.

Bom: You choose differently when you're rested. Kinder people start looking more attractive than exciting ones.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Love from a full cup. Yours refills with {helper_el}.

peer.title: What keeps you steady in love: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Your chart already has plenty of nourishment on paper, so the fix is more of your own element, {helper_el}. Saju reads that as peers.

Bom: In love, that means equals. Friends who'll tell you the truth about who you're dating.

Yeon: The friend who says "they're not good for you" and then still comes to your birthday when you ignore them.

Bom: And a partner who feels like your teammate, not your rescuer.

Yeon: Love between equals is less dramatic and much more fun.

Bom: And notice who's in your corner already. Thank them. They're part of your love life too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: {helper_el} steadies you. Date an equal. Keep honest friends close.

output.title: Where your extra love should go: {helper_el}
output.text:
A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element you naturally give out.

Yeon: Translation: when your strength has nowhere to go, it turns into control. In love, that's the controlling partner.

Bom: So give it somewhere to go. Make things together, play, laugh. Create something that isn't the relationship itself.

Yeon: Couples who make things together fight less about who's in charge.

Bom: Your love is strong. Let it come out as play instead of pressure.

Yeon: Dance badly in the kitchen. Start a ridiculous project together. Strength that plays doesn't need to boss.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your outlet is {helper_el}. Turn strength into play, not control.

wealth.title: What grounds you in love: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Your chart is strong and already expressive, so the fix is {helper_el}, the element you shape and work with.

Bom: In love, that means showing up in concrete ways. Plans that happen. Promises that get kept.

Yeon: You have plenty of charm and plenty of talk. What calms you is doing.

Bom: Book the dinner. Turn up on time. Follow through on the weekend away.

Yeon: Words are lovely. Kept promises are lovelier.

Bom: The person who always books the table ends up being the person they trust.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: {helper_el} grounds you. Less charm. More follow-through.

wood.text:
In real life, {helper_el} in love means growing together. Learn something side by side. Go on long walks. Plant something in a pot on the balcony and argue about watering it.

Bom: Couples who grow together stay curious about each other.

Yeon: Which is exactly what the next chapter is about: how you show love versus how you need it. They're not the same.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood in love: grow something together. Even a basil plant.

fire.text:
In real life, {helper_el} in love means warmth and visibility. Telling them out loud. Holding hands in public. Laughing until it hurts.

Bom: Warm people feel secure. Secure people love better.

Yeon: Next chapter, how you show love versus how you need it. Prepare for a mismatch.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire in love: say it out loud. In public. Often.

earth.text:
In real life, {helper_el} in love means routine and reliability. The Sunday breakfast. The goodnight text. Remembering their mum's birthday.

Bom: Boring rituals are what love actually rests on.

Yeon: Not glamorous. Deeply effective. Next chapter, how you show love, and what you actually need back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth in love: same breakfast every Sunday. Boring. Perfect.

metal.text:
In real life, {helper_el} in love means clarity. Clear yeses, clear nos, clear plans. Saying exactly what you want.

Yeon: Most relationship problems are just vague communication with good intentions.

Bom: Next chapter, how you show love and how you need it. Clarity helps there too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal in love: say the clear yes and the clear no. Vague kills.

water.text:
In real life, {helper_el} in love means depth and rest. Quiet evenings. Long talks. Time alone so you come back with something to share.

Bom: Rested people love more gently.

Yeon: Next chapter, how you show love versus how you need it. Sit somewhere comfy.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water in love: long talks, quiet nights, real rest.

rat.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rat, 子, midwinter Water.

Bom: Up close, you're quick, funny and far more emotional than your public self.

Yeon: And private about it. Getting into your real feelings takes a password, two-factor authentication and a security question.

Bom: Once you trust someone, you're fiercely loyal.

Yeon: The trust bit just takes a while. Hand someone a key early. Your burrow is lovely inside, and almost nobody gets invited.

Rat is a charm branch too, peach blossom in saju. Interest is rarely your problem. Choosing well is.

Bom: Give the person who's kind on a dull Tuesday as much credit as the one who dazzles on a Saturday.

Yeon: And yes, you're more sensitive than you let on. They'd like to know. Next chapter, jealousy. The Rat has opinions.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat at home: witty, private, fiercely loyal. Hand someone the key early.

ox.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth with Metal stored inside.

Yeon: Up close, you're loyal, steady and stubborn about how home should run.

Bom: You make a partner feel completely safe.

Yeon: Safe, and slightly unable to move a single piece of furniture without a fortnight of negotiation.

Ox is a storehouse branch. You store feelings like tins in a cupboard. Then one day the cupboard opens and everything falls out.

Bom: Open the cupboard more often. One feeling at a time.

Yeon: Also, they're allowed to move the sofa. It's their sofa too. Next, jealousy. You'll be surprised how much is stored there too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox at home: loyal, steady, immovable sofa. Open the feelings cupboard weekly.

tiger.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire inside.

Bom: Up close, you're passionate and protective. Dating you is one long adventure.

Yeon: And you get restless the second it starts to feel like routine. Suddenly you need "space."

Tiger is a travel branch, the moving horse in saju. Restlessness is built in. Sometimes it's a real need. Sometimes it's boredom looking for an exit.

Bom: Tell your partner when you feel it, before you act on it.

Yeon: Restless isn't the same as unhappy. Check which one it is before you decide anything. Then book a trip together instead of alone. Next chapter: what makes the Tiger jealous.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger at home: adventure, then restless. Say "I'm twitchy" before you vanish.

rabbit.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood.

Yeon: Up close, you're soft, romantic, and allergic to conflict. You'll redecorate before you'll argue.

Bom: You make home feel beautiful.

Yeon: Beautiful, with one unspoken argument hiding behind every cushion.

Rabbit is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju. People fall for you easily, so you've rarely had to fight for love. Which makes fighting in love feel terrifying.

Bom: A small disagreement won't break anything. Try one.

Yeon: The cushions will survive an argument. So will you. Next chapter, jealousy. Rabbits get it quietly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rabbit at home: gorgeous cushions, hidden arguments. Have one small fight.

dragon.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth.

Bom: Up close, you dream big. You want a love that feels epic.

Yeon: And you've never told them. They're failing an exam they didn't know they were sitting.

Dragon is a storehouse branch. Hopes, hurts and expectations go in. They rarely come out in words.

Bom: Tell them what epic looks like to you. Specifically.

Yeon: "Plan me a surprise weekend" is specific. "I just want you to know me" is a riddle. Nobody can meet expectations they've never been told about. Not even someone wonderful.

Bom: Next chapter, the jealousy you keep behind that big calm face.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dragon at home: epic hopes, never said aloud. Hand over the exam answers.

snake.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal inside.

Yeon: Up close, you notice everything, reveal little and remember all of it.

Bom: You're deeply perceptive. Your partner feels truly seen.

Yeon: Also slightly watched. You clocked the change in their tone three weeks before they did.

Snake is a travel branch. Calm on the outside, restless underneath.

Bom: Share what you notice, gently, when you notice it.

Noticing is a gift. Keeping a file is a hobby. Pick the gift.

Yeon: Don't save it for the argument. Next chapter, jealousy. You're very good at it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snake at home: you notice everything. Share it now, not mid-fight.

horse.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire.

Bom: Up close, you're warm, passionate and generous. Loving you feels like a long summer.

Yeon: And you gallop. Fast start, fast exit the second it feels like a fence.

Horse is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju. Easy to fall for, hard to keep.

Bom: Slow the start down. Stay longer in the middle.

The fence you feel is often just a Tuesday. Stay for a few more Tuesdays.

Yeon: The middle is where love gets good. Next chapter, jealousy. Horses kick.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse at home: summer love, fast exits. Stay for the middle.

goat.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth with Wood stored inside.

Yeon: Up close, you're a nurturer who worries in silence and sighs meaningfully.

Bom: You look after everyone at home.

Yeon: And hope someone looks after you back without you having to say it.

Goat is a storehouse branch. Your needs go into storage, and they come out as sighs.

Bom: Say one need a day. In words. No sighing.

A sigh can mean twelve things. A sentence means one. Pick the sentence.

Yeon: Next, jealousy. You do it with a very specific sigh.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Goat at home: nurtures everyone, sighs instead of asking. Use words.

monkey.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water.

Bom: Up close, you're playful and clever. Being with you is never boring.

Yeon: And the moment it gets serious, you do a bit. Every single time.

Monkey is a travel branch. You keep moving so nothing heavy lands on you.

Bom: Let one serious conversation happen without a joke.

The jokes are wonderful. They're just better after the serious bit, not instead of it.

Yeon: Just one serious talk. Then you can do a bit. Next chapter: jealousy, and the bit you do to hide it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Monkey at home: hilarious, slippery. One serious chat a week, no jokes.

rooster.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal.

Yeon: Up close, you're sharp, stylish, and running a quality-control department.

Bom: You care about doing love well.

Yeon: You care about doing it perfectly. And your partner starts to feel like a draft with comments.

Rooster is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju. People are drawn to your polish. Let them see the unpolished version too.

Bom: Let one imperfection slide each day.

Nobody relaxes in a home that's being graded. Put the red pen down.

Yeon: On purpose. Next chapter, jealousy. You'll critique that too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rooster at home: love with tracked changes. Let one thing slide.

dog.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth with Fire stored inside.

Bom: Up close, you're loyal to the bone. Once someone's in, you'd fight anyone for them.

Yeon: Getting in, though. Partners do a year of probation and a background check.

Dog is a storehouse branch. Slights and kindnesses all get stored, carefully.

Bom: Shorten the probation. Good people get tired at the gate.

Yeon: Loyalty is your superpower. Suspicion is just its overprotective cousin. Next chapter, jealousy. The guard dog has thoughts.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dog at home: loyal forever, after a year of probation. Shorten it.

pig.text:
The animal of your birth day is the you only a partner gets to see. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood.

Yeon: Up close, you're generous, romantic and a world-class excuser of bad behaviour.

Bom: You see the best in people.

Yeon: You see the best in people who forgot your birthday twice.

Pig is a travel branch. Part of you is always dreaming of somewhere else, and that softens how hard you look at what's here.

Bom: Look clearly. Kindness and a free pass aren't the same thing.

Yeon: Kindness that never says "that's not okay" ends up being kind to everyone but you. Next chapter, jealousy. Even Pigs get it. They just excuse it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig at home: generous, romantic, excuses everything. Stop excusing.

day_branch_heading: Who you are once love moves in: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

fast.speaker: yeon
fast.text: Fast and hard, you said. So you've named the kids by date three. Let's check the brakes.

slow.speaker: bom
slow.text: Slowly, then all at once. The prettiest way to fall, and the scariest one.

overthink.speaker: yeon
overthink.text: "I don't fall, I overthink." You do fall. You just do it in your head first, for months, alone.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You didn't say how you fall. That's fine. Your birthday already told on you.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

gye-water.how-you-fall:
You fall through feeling. A look, a song, a moment where they seemed to get you. And you're gone, quietly.

Bom: Your intuition about people is usually right.

Yeon: Your intuition is right. Your timing is a crime. You wait so long they meet someone who said it first.

Bom: Say a small version of it early. "I like talking to you." That's all it takes.
gye-water.flirting:
Bom: Your quiet flirting is very romantic.

Yeon: Your quiet flirting is a state secret. Four months of meaningful looks, and they thought you were shy about the weather.

You flirt with feeling. A song you send. A meaningful look. A perfectly timed text.

Bom: Every gesture is full of meaning.

Yeon: Meaning nobody can read without a decoder ring.

Add one plain sentence. "I really like you."

Bom: Your depth deserves to be seen.

Yeon: And heard. Out loud. With actual words.
gye-water.attachment:
You attach silently and deeply.

Yeon: You've imagined the whole future. They know your coffee order.

Bom: Your love runs so deep.

Yeon: Deep enough that you never quite let it surface.

When they pull away, you don't say anything. You just quietly start leaving.

Bom: That's self-protection.

Yeon: That's leaving before they can. Tell them you noticed. "You seem far away. Are we okay?"
gye-water.jealousy:
Your jealousy is invisible.

Yeon: You feel it intensely and show nothing. Then you go a bit distant for a week.

Bom: Needy is the last thing you want to seem.

Yeon: So you seem cold. Worse option.

Your trigger is feeling unseen. Like they don't notice your feelings.

Bom: Say "I felt a bit left out tonight."

Yeon: Simple. Five seconds. Saves a week of silent drifting.
gye-water.red-flag:
You disappear.

Yeon: Something hurts, and you quietly fade out of the relationship. They don't know why.

Bom: You hate confrontation.

Yeon: So much that ending it feels easier than one hard sentence.

The flag: leaving instead of speaking.

Bom: Stay one minute longer than feels comfortable.

Yeon: Say the hard thing in that minute. That minute is where relationships are saved.
gye-water.what-you-need:
You need someone who notices.

Bom: Who sees when you're quiet and asks why. Gently.

Yeon: Who doesn't need you to explain everything. But keeps asking anyway.

Bom: You need someone patient with your silences.

Yeon: Someone who makes it safe to talk. Who never makes you regret opening up.

You need tenderness and attention.

Bom: Someone who sees the rain and brings an umbrella. And then stands under it with you.

gye-water.speaker: bom
gye-water.text: You love like rain. Soft, quiet, soaking into everything.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: You've had a whole relationship with them. In your head. They were great in it.

gye-water.speaker: bom
gye-water.text: You fall in silence. You feel it everywhere before you say a word.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: The playlist was not obvious, Rain. Say the plain sentence.

gye-water.speaker: bom
gye-water.text: Don't quietly leave first, Gye. Ask the question.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Distant for a week, Rain? Say "I felt left out" instead.

spring.intro: Spring rain. You feed everything around you without anyone noticing it was you. You sense moods, fix vibes, water other people's plants. Quietly essential. Quietly forgotten. Not anymore.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Everything grows a little when you're around.

summer.intro: Rain in summer, gone the moment it lands. You chase what you want in quiet, clever ways, and you vanish when a room gets too loud. People find you fascinating. They also never quite know where you went.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You left the party without saying bye. Again. Iconic.

autumn.intro: Autumn rain, fed by cool clean air. Intuitive to the point of spooky. You know who's lying, who's sad, and who's about to text before your phone even lights up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut is right more often than your decisions are.

winter.intro: Winter rain. Double water. Still, deep, mostly internal. You feel everything at full volume and show about four percent of it. Your notes app has more emotional range than most novels.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your quiet isn't empty. It's full.

earth.intro: Rain falling on hard ground. Born in the soil weeks, so you met walls early: rules, expectations, people who didn't get you. You learned to soak in slowly instead of crashing through. Patient. Persistent. Underrated.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fight walls. You just wear them down. Over years.

gye-water.strong:
Built strong, Gye. Intuition so well fed you think you're psychic.

Yeon: You decide what your partner feels without asking. Then you react to your guess.

Bom: Your intuition is often right.

Yeon: Often. Not always. And they get blamed for subtext they never wrote.

Ask before you assume. "Are you upset with me?"

Bom: Even wise people check.

Yeon: Your guess is a hypothesis, not a verdict. Test it with one question.
gye-water.weak:
Built soft, Gye. Gentle rain with nowhere to land.

Yeon: In love you absorb their moods and forget your own.

Bom: You're so empathetic.

Yeon: Empathetic to the point of disappearing.

Protect one evening a week for just you.

Bom: Rain can pool for you too, Gye.

Yeon: If you can't tell whose feelings you're carrying, put them all down for an evening. Then pick up only yours.

love-language.text:
You show love through presence, Gye. Quiet company, deep understanding, knowing what they need before they say it.

Bom: Being loved by you feels like being understood without words.

Yeon: And you need exactly that back. Which is a lot to expect from someone who isn't psychic.

What you need is to feel seen. Noticed. Asked about.

Bom: And gentleness. Patience while you find your words.

Yeon: Tell them. "I feel loved when you ask how I really am." Then answer honestly when they do.

Bom: Being seen starts with letting them look. And when they get it right, say so. It teaches them how to love you.

Yeon: Next chapter, my red flag report. You can read it quietly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You love through quiet presence, Gye. Let them ask, then answer honestly.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They're not psychic. Tell them how to see you.

good-week.heading: Your good week in love
good-week.text:
One quiet evening together, phones away.

One moment where they asked how you really were.

One feeling you said out loud.

One small disagreement you stayed for.

Plus a rainy day under a blanket.

Bom: If your week has those, you'll feel seen and safe.

Yeon: Reread chapter three in a month. If they know you like them, I'll be very proud. Quietly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your good week: one quiet night, one feeling said, one blanket.

the-fight.text:
You don't fight, Gye. You evaporate.

Yeon: They say something hurtful, and you go quiet, then quieter, then you're gone. Emotionally, then sometimes literally.

Bom: You just hate conflict.

Yeon: You hate it so much you'll leave a whole relationship instead of having one argument.

And they don't even know what happened.

Bom: Say the hurt. One sentence. "That really hurt me." If talking feels impossible, write it down and hand it over. Words on paper still count.

Yeon: Then stay for the answer. Next chapter: the blind spot that makes you vanish.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Evaporating isn't a fight style, Gye. It's an exit.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: One sentence about the hurt. Then stay for what comes back.

gye-water.title: You fell for them three months ago. They still have no idea.
gye-water.text:
You fall inside. Daydreams, playlists, a whole imagined future. Meanwhile, out loud, you've said "haha same" four times.

Bom: Your love is so deep.

Yeon: Your love is so deep it's never surfaced.
gye-water.end: Yeon: How you fall is invisible. Making it visible is on the next page.

cliff.gye-water: Yeon: Your flirting style, Rain: so quiet it's | practically classified. You think the playlist was obvious. It was not obvious.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Red flag: you'd rather leave quietly than say one uncomfortable thing.
